correctness.rationale: Ideals correspond bijectively to nonempty proper supports and adjacency is nonempty support intersection. A two-vertex total dominating set must be adjacent and must cover every coordinate, because an uncovered singleton-support ideal would meet neither selected ideal. Conversely an intersecting pair whose union is all coordinates dominates every nonempty support and its two selected vertices dominate each other. Such a two-set is automatically paired. Counting ordered pairs amounts to surjections of the r coordinates onto the three nonempty classes A\B, B\A and A intersect B, giving 3^r-3*2^r+3, then dividing by the fixed-point-free swap. The r=2 graph is two isolated vertices. The frozen verifier exhausts r<=7 and agrees with this all-r proof.

final_claim: For a product of r fields, the ideal-intersection graph has no total or paired dominating set at r=2; for r>=3 both minimum parameters equal two, the minimum sets are exactly intersecting proper support pairs covering all coordinates, and their number is (3^r-3*2^r+3)/2.
